candidate.answerReason: The circle graph has one unshaded half and two equal patterned quarters. Only C has equal patterned bars and an unshaded bar twice as tall.

methods.label: Match the proportions
methods.explanation:
The unshaded region is half the circle. The dotted and gridded regions each occupy one quarter, so their amounts are equal, and the unshaded amount is twice either patterned amount.

The matching bar graph must therefore have equal dotted and gridded bars, with the unshaded bar twice their height. D and E have unequal patterned bars. In B the unshaded bar is shorter than the patterned bars, while in A it is taller but less than twice as tall. C has exactly the required proportions, so the answer is \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
methods.levelReason: The solution uses halves, quarters, equal quantities, and twice-as-tall comparisons, appropriate for AMC 8.
